02 · Productivity Setup

Select the operating model first. Clicking a model applies it immediately to the current service-order queue; there is no separate Apply action.

1 POINT = 1 STANDARD HOUR
Core rule. The baremo is the standard quantity of work. Technology changes the resource mix, supervision span and scalable capacity; it never erases the standard point.

Service-order result

The selected productivity model is applied immediately to every released service order and its Human / Digital point split is recalculated live.

Productivity baremo

Edit standard minutes or the economic rate. Standard points remain the common unit of work and feed both Warehouse execution and Delivery planning.

#Route stageTaskEvidenceStandard minPoints€/h€/unit

What each productivity indicator means

Read the model as capacity allocation, not as a redefinition of the standard work.

Standard work pointsThe baremo quantity of work. 1 point = 1 standard hour. Technology does not change it.
Human workloadThe share of standard work requiring a Human Operational Agent.
Digital workloadThe share executed by AI, automation, robotics or digitally assisted work.
Supervision capacityThe number of concurrent digital or robotic agents a human can supervise under the selected model.

04 · Productivity & Satisfaction Report i

Connect execution evidence with post-order NPS to evaluate Operational Agents, service orders and development actions without losing the distinction between productivity and customer experience.

P · NPS · AGENT · ORDER · DEVELOPMENT
ACADEMIC IDEAProductivity and satisfaction answer different questions.P compares standard work with actual resource hours. NPS captures how the customer evaluated the completed order.
BRIDGEOrder ID connects the two evidence layers.The order is the safest operational bridge. Customer ID is used only as a fallback when it identifies a single order.
INTERPRETATIONAssociation is not causality.An agent can be associated with an order's NPS signal for teaching and management review, but the NPS result may reflect many parts of the experience.
MANAGEMENT OUTPUTClassify, then choose an action.The combined score supports a development action: Learning, Compliance or Excellence.

METHODOLOGY AT THE END OF THE JOURNEY

DIIIP explains why operational evidence creates value

Orders, workload, routes, suppliers and delivery evidence become structured inputs for measurable productivity, service quality and economic decisions.

D
Data

Orders, customer keys, SPO priority, baremos, SLA commitments, vehicle data, route events and delivery evidence.

I
Information

The data is structured by operational stage, agent, route, supplier, vehicle, order and delivery state.

I
Intelligence

Rules interpret productivity, economic guardrails, capacity, route priority and SLA compliance.

I
Insights

The workshop reveals where capacity is released, where cost accumulates and where an operational exception requires attention.

P
Personalization Actions

SPO, customer context and route evidence activate differentiated service, delivery and post-sale actions.

KAI·ROI EQUATION · CUSTOMER EQUITY

This operational system creates execution evidence for the KAI·ROI layer

The workshop does not redefine KAI·ROI. It creates structured operational evidence that can support productivity, ROI, Customer Equity and defensible management decisions.

The formal KAI·ROI structure remains sovereign; this tool focuses on execution evidence.
